title: One more swap
topic: Rotas, leave, and training versus service
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in orthopaedics. You've covered three extra night shifts this month and feel tired. Dr Lewis, another F2, asks you to swap so he can attend a job interview next week. The swap would give you another night shift.

He says no one else can do it.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Agree, provided the swap keeps you within your rest requirements.
options.detailed: Checking the rules is sensible, but you are already tired, and another night may not be wise even if it's allowed.

options.text: Tell him his interview isn't your problem.
options.detailed: You aren't obliged to swap, but this is dismissive of a colleague. It ranks above working while tired because it doesn't put patients at risk.

options.text: Suggest he asks the rota coordinator for help.
options.detailed: The rota coordinator may know who is available. It ranks second because it's less personal than offering to help.

options.text: Say you can't do another night, and offer to help find cover.
options.brief: Honest about your limits while still trying to help.
options.detailed: You're tired after extra nights. Saying so honestly, and helping him find cover, supports him without risking your own fitness to work.

options.text: Agree to the swap, despite how tired you are.
options.brief: Risks your health and patient safety.
options.detailed: Wanting to help is good, but taking on another night when you're already tired puts patients at risk. It is the least appropriate option.

explanation.issue: This tests whether you look after your own wellbeing while still supporting a colleague.
explanation.keyDetails: You've covered three extra nights. He needs the swap for an interview. He says no one else can do it.
explanation.reasoning: [D] is honest and helpful, [C] points him to the coordinator, and [A] helps cautiously. [B] is unkind, and [E] risks patient safety.
explanation.competing: Some would see [A] as best. It ranks third because you're already tired, even if the swap is within the rules.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 1, making sure fatigue doesn't put patients at risk.
